newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures close lower on slow cash.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures close lower on slow cash.

text.p: Although CME lumber futures found early support on continued labor concerns in British Columbia, the market drifted lower into the close following the continued slow cash market, traders said.
Lumber closed $4.60 per tbf lower to $1.00 higher with only distant July up. September was off most at $342.00 and November off $0.60 at $342.60 per tbf.

Reports of very slow wholesale and retail lumber business weighed on the market after early carryover demand over labor unrest in British Columbia. Demand lacked followthrough as interest for wood continued lighter than expected, they said.
